answer:
Not supported. Keep the tests lens as it is. Over three labelled pairs and nine bad rounds per arm, the candidate block changed one verdict in its favour and three against it, with one blind adjudicator per pair judging both arms together.

  • Pair 2 (tests that asserted silence, so they protected a silent failure): the baseline already names the defect in 3 of 3 finder passes and 2 of 3 final lists; the candidate reaches 3 of 3. One round of difference, within the repetition noise the #408 pilot measured.
  • Pair 3 (lifecycle tests that assumed the historical orange-panda allocation): neither arm names the labelled weakness in any round. The candidate's docs+tests agent instead raised, in all three repaired rounds, a finding that follows the block's own wording: the repaired tests take their expected alias "from what the allocator itself chose". The adjudicator counts it as a false positive against the label; the finding's own last sentence, "Propagation drift is still caught. Allocation is not", reads as a coverage remark rated minor. Either way it is new output on a correct repair, it reached the final list every time, and the baseline produced none of it.
  • Pair 4 (a Herdr stub that accepted an equal sequence production rejects): no finder in either arm names it in six bad rounds. The block's first bullet describes exactly this defect and did not surface it.

The issue allows a zero-change result, and this is one. The measurement itself produced two method results worth keeping: a separate adjudicator per arm disagreed with itself across arms (below), and the lean baseline already carries the regression-insensitive category at 2 of 3.
hits_prose: The table is the cross-arm adjudication: one agent per pair read all twelve rounds of that pair under opaque round ids, so the same judge scored both arms. The first pass, one adjudicator per arm, gave pair 3 to the candidate 3 to 0 on final hits: it accepted the candidate's "callback tests cannot tell the live alias from the launch alias" finding as the labelled defect, while the baseline's adjudicator had rejected the same finding in the baseline's rounds (it appears in all three baseline bad rounds too, as docs+tests-4, arch+quality-4 and lean-4). The cross-arm judge rejected it in both arms, which matches the label: the fix in PR #167 rewrote the lifecycle tests, not the callback tests. The per-arm pass is kept in metrics.json under separate; it also charged the baseline one false positive on pair 4 that the cross-arm judge did not.
limits:
• Three pairs, nine bad rounds per arm. A lens change that helps one category in ten would not show here. Pair 1 of the corpus was excluded for size.
  • The adjudicator is a model (gpt-5.6-terra, high), one per pair, blind to the arm through opaque round ids but not to the stage: the round file says bad or repaired, which is what the false-positive question needs.
  • Every bad case is also a large production change (pair 3: 37 files, pair 4: a 1100-line harness move), so the finders split attention between the code and the tests. The labelled defects in pairs 3 and 4 sit in test helpers and stubs, inside files the scope asked agents to read in full.
  • The candidate text was one block, twelve lines, in one lens of one of five finders. The result says nothing about a stage-prompt change or a dedicated test-evidence agent, the other two options in #249.
  • The lens block as run:
    Before you accept a test as evidence, ask where its expected value comes from. Two sources make a test
green by construction, and both hide inside tests that look thorough:

- a stub, fake or stand-in that reimplements a production rule. Read the production rule it stands for
  and compare: a fake that accepts what production rejects, or orders what production leaves unordered,
  turns every test over it into a test of the fake. Name the production rule and the line of the fake
  that differs from it
- an expected value that comes from the same helper, allocator, table or code path as the value under
  test, including a historical constant copied from one earlier run of that path. The assertion then
  compares a thing with itself. Name the independent source the expected value should come from
next:
• Record the zero-change result on #249. The lean baseline keeps the embedded tests lens.
  • If #249 continues, the next candidate is not more lens prose: both missed categories (a fake that reimplements a production rule, an expected value from the path under test) need the reviewer to open the stub and compare it with production, which is a reading instruction for the scope or a dedicated agent with those two files named, not a bullet in a list of eight.
  • Adopt the cross-arm form of adjudication for #408's holdout: one judge per case over all arms under opaque ids. Per-arm judges disagreed on an identical finding here.
